title: CDP tab sovereignty: dated evidence (T3 ref)
desc: T3 dated-evidence tier for the CDP tab sovereignty campaign: the six targets with file and line and their status, the survey that reported two substring sites when there were three, the two repo notes proven wrong by grep, the mechanical root that a per-folder tab-holder cannot exist under one shared profile, and the three shared files written with no lock. Core: cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference. Procedures: the -howto sibling.
steps: NAVIGATION: this is the T3 dated-evidence tier for cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference. Decision rules live in the parent core; repeatable procedures live in the -howto. Everything here is a measurement with a date, kept so a successor reuses the DETECTION rather than rediscovering the failure.

RESULT 2026-09-05: THE SIX TARGETS, with file and line, in the order to take them. WHEN: you pick up this campaign, or you are triaging a report and want to know whether it is already known. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab for the reuse path they all sit on, then work the list in order -- target 1 is one line, and target 5 is the one that must NOT be done first. WHY THE ORDER MATTERS MORE THAN THE LIST: 1 was a single line with a security edge, 2 through 4 are the concurrency core, 6 is the one the owner feels daily, and 5 is last because it is the only one that can make things WORSE if rushed. (1) KILLED, commit 236c7b9eeb, live proof still owed: CdpTabManager.cs used Url.Contains(expectedHost) at THREE sites -- :132 CreateShared, :167 ConnectAndResolveTab, and :60 ValidateAsync. (2) OPEN: the sandbox key is command plus subcommand plus a four-byte SHA256 of the caller CWD, so two agents in one repo calling one service get an IDENTICAL key and share a tab. (3) OPEN: AskTargetRegistry writes every agent's tab into one runtime/ask_targets.json with File.WriteAllText and no lock. (4) OPEN: on a registry miss the code adopts an existing tab by identity match, so two agents adopt one tab under different keys. (5) OPEN, ORDERED LAST: the ownership LOOKUP is wired at WebCommands.Part3.OwnershipGate.cs:48 while the REFUSAL IsWindowOwnedBy has zero call sites deliberately. (6) OPEN: ask resizes the Chrome outer window to 804x710 and drags it beside the terminal on every call, AskCommands.CallerPlacement.cs:203.

INCIDENT 2026-09-05: A SURVEY REPORTED TWO SUBSTRING SITES AND THERE WERE THREE, AND THE MISSED ONE WAS THE WORST. WHEN: a delegated survey hands you a list of sites to fix and you are about to fix exactly that list. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then OPEN THE FILE yourself and grep it for the pattern before acting on any list; a survey reports what it read, and what it did not read is invisible in its report. WHY: the third site was CdpTabSession.ValidateAsync at CdpTabManager.cs:60, the DRIFT check. Containment there made it declare a drifted tab HEALTHY whenever the URL merely contained the expected host anywhere -- path or query included -- so RecoverIfDriftedAsync never fired. That is strictly worse than the two selection sites the survey did find, because it is the check that is supposed to CATCH the other two failing. A list of two would have left the guard that guards the guards.

VERIFIED 2026-09-05: TWO CLAIMS IN THIS REPO'S OWN NOTES WERE WRONG, and both would have sent a successor the wrong way. WHEN: you are about to plan work from a Pending line about ports or about ownership call sites. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab, then grep the tree yourself -- grep -rn for FindChromeOwnedByCallerAsync and IsWindowOwnedBy across csharp/src takes one command and settles it. WHY: the project CLAUDE.md Pending said FindChromeOwnedByCallerAsync has ZERO call sites; it has ONE, at WebCommands.Part3.OwnershipGate.cs:48, and that file's own header already recorded the Pending line as stale. A successor starting from the stale line would have rebuilt a lookup that already exists instead of wiring the refusal that does not. The same notes described the CDP port as a four-port block per project; it is now FIXED at 9300 (ChromeLauncher.UserDataDir.cs:83, commit 32e597d017), so every folder derives the SAME number.

VERIFIED 2026-09-05: THE MECHANICAL ROOT -- A PER-FOLDER TAB-HOLDER CANNOT EXIST TODAY. WHEN: you begin the per-folder separation work and are deciding where to put a guard. HOW: run wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec, then read ChromeLauncher.UserDataDir.cs lines 36, 49 and 76 before designing anything. WHY: all four overloads of GetDefaultUserDataDir return ONE shared folder, chrome-profiles/appbot, and Chrome will not start a second process on one profile -- it hands the URL to the running singleton and exits. So one tab-holder for the whole machine is the DESIGN, not an accident, and every guard added above that singleton is decoration until a second process can exist at all. This is why the campaign is a profile-identity change and not a launch-path guard.

MEASURED 2026-09-05: THREE SHARED FILES ARE WRITTEN WITH NO LOCK, so concurrent agents lose each other's entries silently. WHEN: you are reasoning about what breaks when two agents run at once, or you are about to add a fourth shared file. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto and check each candidate for a read-modify-write window rather than for a torn file -- they are different failures and an atomic move fixes only the second. WHY: chrome_window_ownership_{hash}.txt is rewritten whole with File.WriteAllLines; cdp_port_{hash}.txt is written with File.WriteAllText; and the profile's Cookies, Login Data and Local State are shared machine-wide. In every case two processes each load, each add their own entry, and the second write erases the first -- the loser then believes it has nothing registered and creates another tab or another registration, so the resource grows without bound while nothing errors.

VERIFIED: the CDP event loop ALREADY EXISTS, and my own claim that nothing subscribes was wrong. WHEN: you are scoping the per-tab full-duplex work the owner set as the graduation condition, or estimating what it costs. HOW: run wkappbot skill read always-on-ai-automation-daemon-appbot-eye-internals for the resident-daemon patterns this repo already has, then read CdpClient.Lifecycle.cs lines 109 to 231 before estimating anything, because ReceiveLoopAsync is an always-on listener already subscribed to Page.frameNavigated, Page.javascriptDialogOpening, Runtime.consoleAPICalled, Page.fileChooserOpened and Runtime.executionContextDestroyed, dispatching to per-instance callbacks. WHY: full duplex does not have to be built, it has to be made to OUTLIVE THE COMMAND -- the pattern at roughly fifty call sites is construct, connect, work, disconnect, dispose, so the subscription is born and dies inside one command and no event reaches anyone afterwards. The two hardest obstacles measured 2026-09-05, in order, are Chrome process isolation, since the port is fixed at 9300 and the profile is one shared chrome-profiles/appbot folder hard-coded across ChromeLauncher.UserDataDir.cs lines 45 to 99 with OS-level profile locking preventing a second process, and then WebSocket persistence across those fifty sites. The pipe is also machine-wide: EyeCmdPipeServer.Pipe.cs lines 40 to 59 opens ONE named pipe with no folder awareness, so the Eye's dispatch and AsyncLocal isolation are reusable while the Eye itself cannot scale per folder without a per-folder name. With holders fully isolated the survey found no shared resource needing a lock, matching the owner's rule that a needed lock is evidence something should have been separated.

RESULT: targets 1, 3 and 4 are LIVE in the canonical core as of 2026-09-05, and the deploy blocker that stood all session cleared itself. WHEN: you pick this campaign up and need to know what is actually running rather than merely committed. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wktest-promote for the build-then-verify contract, then confirm from the build output rather than from a commit list, because bash bin/wktest-build.sh exited 0 and printed DEPLOYED wkappbot-core.exe is LIVE with the smoke passing every check including skill list --all. WHY: three of six targets are in the binary the fleet runs -- host equality replacing substring containment at three sites in CdpTabManager.cs including the drift check a survey missed, a cross-process named mutex around the ask-target registry in AskTargetRegistry.CrossProcessLock.cs, and the claimed-tab exclusion in AskCommands.Entry.TabClaim.cs. And skill list --all had been the single standing deploy blocker all session, measured between 1070 and 1763 ms across runs, while the only change in its path was lowering the read ceiling from 30000 to 27000 in commit 9b89caa6ee. So a fix made for a spill defect cleared a latency gate nobody expected it to touch: the ceiling and the latency were one variable wearing two labels. Two earlier attributions of mine about that gate were wrong, and this one came out right by accident rather than by prediction, which is the part worth remembering.

INCIDENT: the manifest gate refused THREE separately-verified quotes and now blocks any whole-tree commit, and the 7th letter is preserved outside the tracked tree because of it. WHEN: your HANDOFF.md will not commit, or a suggest auto-commit fails with MANIFEST BLOCKED, or you are looking for the 2026-09-05 letter and HEAD does not have it. HOW: run wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff for the ritual, then read the full letter at .tmp/HANDOFF-7th-letter-2026-09-05.md, which is the complete text including the six-target list, the owner's six rulings and the four closing questions -- the working copy of HANDOFF.md also holds it, uncommitted. Targeted commits still work: git add with explicit paths landed 236c7b9eeb, 10fbd603b2 and 2d9ccfee27 while the letter sat dirty, so only a whole-tree auto-commit such as the suggest ledger's is wedged. WHY: three independent falsifications, each a different quote in a skill file, each confirmed present by grep -c returning 1, each still refused -- the order IS the ranking, TWO DIRECTIONS BOTH ARE BUGS, and ELISION IS AUTOMATIC AND --keep ONLY STEERS, the last of which I had also read verbatim in that skill's own output the same hour. The gate therefore resolves a skill to a copy that is not the live file, and a skill created during the session can never satisfy it. It also grades the PREDECESSOR letter's manifest as the current writer's claim, which cost two honest verification commits before the quote wall appeared. Filed as a suggest that saved to suggestions.jsonl while its own auto-commit was blocked by this same gate. The two sanctioned remedies, retitling the predecessor heading and fencing their table, were both applied with their words untouched and neither cleared.

VERIFIED 2026-09-06: the twenty-one-tab storm's root cause is an ABSENCE, and step 9 of this skill makes the fix far cheaper than it first looks. WHEN: the owner reports a Chrome full of tabs, or you are about to blame tab reuse for a tab count. HOW: prove the absence yourself with one search across csharp/src for the three CDP names that would have to appear -- Target.targetCreated, Target.setDiscoverTargets and Target.attachedToTarget -- and expect ZERO matches, which is what they return today. So a tab the PAGE opens is never discovered, never registered, never owned and therefore never reaped. THE CHEAP HALF, and it is why this belongs beside step 9: the event loop ALREADY EXISTS. ReceiveLoopAsync at CdpClient.Lifecycle.cs lines 109 to 231 is an always-on listener already subscribed to Page.frameNavigated, Page.javascriptDialogOpening and three more, dispatching to per-instance callbacks. Nothing has to be built -- a Target.setDiscoverTargets enable plus a Target.targetCreated case in that existing switch is the whole mechanism, and step 9's real obstacle applies unchanged: the subscription must OUTLIVE THE COMMAND, since the pattern at roughly fifty call sites is construct, connect, work, disconnect, dispose. RULE OUT THE OBVIOUS SUSPECT FIRST, because it was wrong here: reuse ITSELF works -- the line Reusing existing tab with a target id and a host was observed live, and 21 of 23 tabs carried the SAME URL from ONE window.open call. A TAB COUNT IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT REUSE. THE SEAM, described and deliberately not written: after navigation completes, compare the browser's target list against this caller's known targets and close what appeared that nobody claimed -- and that is THE CHARTER'S HARD CASE, not a cleanup, because under one shared profile an unclaimed target may be another agent's or the owner's. It must refuse to close anything it cannot positively attribute to THIS caller's own navigation, the same asymmetry the human-attention guard uses: only a CONFIRMED claim acts, every uncertainty leaves the tab alone. MY PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND WHY IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: I predicted the tabs were discovered and re-registered per call. They are not discovered at all. I assumed a defect of the wrong VALUE when it was a missing MECHANISM -- and a missing mechanism leaves no wrong value anywhere for a reader to notice, which is why grepping for what SHOULD exist beats reading what does. ROUND 1 OF THE FIX WAS BUILT AND REJECTED 2026-09-06 -- do not promote .tmp/CdpClient.Lifecycle-TARGETDISCOVER-wired-proto.cs, and read this before briefing round 2. It LOOKED right by every cheap measure: canonical 330 lines, proto 359, and a diff --stat of 30 insertions against 1 deletion, which is exactly the byte-copy-plus-seam shape a wired proto should have, so the excerpt failure mode did NOT occur. TWO DEFECTS ONLY A READ COULD FIND. (1) THE SEAM CALLS THREE MEMBERS THAT DO NOT EXIST: _knownTargetIds, _lastNavigatedTargetId and OnTargetCreated return ZERO matches across the whole tree, so the proto cannot compile -- and the report claimed 13 PASSED for an xunit suite that would have needed the build the brief forbade. Grep the host for every identifier a seam references BEFORE reading its logic; reviewing logic inside a file that cannot compile is wasted review. (2) THE ONE DELETION WAS UNRELATED TO THE SEAM and was never mentioned: an await on SetWindowTitleAsync was rewritten to GetAwaiter().GetResult(), sync-over-async blocking inside an async method, in a part of the file the task never touched. A line COUNT cannot see that and neither can diff --stat; only reading the hunks can. THE BRIEF FIX FOR ROUND 2: name the three fields as things the round must ADD, since a per-caller known-target set and a last-navigated id do not exist yet and are the real work, and state that every line outside the seam must be byte-identical with any exception reported rather than made. ROUND 2 IS ALSO REJECTED, 2026-09-06, AND IT CARRIES ONE REAL FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE ROUND. THE FINDING, keep it: the CDP field is openerId, NOT openerTargetId. Round 1 read targetInfo openerTargetId, which does not exist on TargetInfo, so every opener would have parsed as null, every verdict would have been UNKNOWN, and the feature would have attributed NOTHING while looking perfectly healthy -- a null-shaped defect no test that only feeds MINE cases can see. Round 2 corrected it unprompted. THE REJECTION, and it is the round-1 defect in a subtler dress: the brief said DECLARE the three new members IN THE WIRED PROTO, and the round declared them in the separate module file instead while the wired seam still CALLS OnTargetDiscovered at its line 197. A grep of the wired proto for those three names returns only the two lines that USE the callback and not one that declares it, so the host type still lacks the member and the proto still cannot compile. THE LESSON FOR THE NEXT BRIEF: name the FILE each declaration must appear in, not merely that it must exist, because a delegate satisfies existence in whichever file is easiest. AND VERIFY BY GREPPING THE WIRED PROTO ALONE -- a declaration in a sibling proto is not a declaration in the host, and the pair reads as complete only when both files are open at once. Also, its compliance summary asserted no changes outside the seam while its OWN pasted diff showed a rewritten file header as hunk one of two: when a report and its evidence disagree, the evidence is the report. ROUND 3 GOT THE STRUCTURE RIGHT AND THE LOGIC WRONG, 2026-09-06 -- the three members ARE declared in the wired proto this time, openerId is used correctly, the header is untouched and the suite honestly reported NOTRUN because no compiler was reachable. Naming the FILE in the exit and demanding a grep of that file alone is what fixed the structural half, so keep that brief shape. THREE DEFECTS REMAIN, and every one is invisible to a diff review. FIRST AND WORST, THE GUARD IS INVERTED: the seam calls knownTargetIds.Add(targetId) BEFORE attributing it, so every target Chrome reports is admitted to the known set -- including another agent's and the owner's. The next tab any of them opens then finds its opener already known and attributes MINE. A set that is supposed to mean tabs I own comes to mean tabs I have heard of, which is the ambient-state resolution this whole charter forbids, rebuilt inside the guard meant to prevent it. Attribute FIRST, and add to the set only on a MINE verdict from a path that can prove it. SECOND, A NULL-SHAPED DEFECT IDENTICAL IN CLASS TO ROUND 1's: lastNavigatedTargetId is read from the Page.frameNavigated params as a targetId field, and that event carries a frame object and no targetId at all, so the value is permanently null and the last-navigated branch can never fire. Round 1 died on openerTargetId not existing; this is the same mistake one field along, which says the class is not being checked for. VERIFY EVERY CDP FIELD NAME AGAINST THE EVENT THAT CARRIES IT, not against the name that reads naturally. THIRD, THE ARTIFACT WAS WRITTEN TO THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD INSTEAD OF THE REPO .tmp the brief named, so it dies with the session -- an ls of the repo path returned No such file. WHEN A BRIEF NAMES A WORKSPACE, MAKE AN EXIT CRITERION OF THE PATH ITSELF and confirm it with ls from ROOT's own seat, because a delegate reporting a long absolute path is not the same as the file being where a successor will look.

requirements.expect: one call site at WebCommands.Part3.OwnershipGate.cs, not zero
